title: Contextual fidelity prober for FP8/INT8 calibration and automated acceptance
creator: Asha Mehta
description:
Goal: Build an automated prober that runs targeted fidelity checks for FP8 and INT8 quantized model variants against contextual golden families and emits deterministic pass/fail gates for rollouts. The prober must 1) support per-cohort golden prompts (short/long/formal/chatty), 2) compute multi-metric signatures (token-level KL, top-1 token divergence, n-gram overlap, generation log-likelihood shift, and semantic similarity), 3) aggregate results into cohort-aware pass/fail decisions with adaptive thresholds that account for prompt length and model temperature.

Scope:
- In-scope: ingest calibration profiles (quantization parameters), run golden-family replay across representative contexts, compute and store per-request metrics, evaluate gate logic, and emit detailed telemetry for Console.
- Out-of-scope: full rollout orchestration automation (handled by Runtime rollout), large-scale golden curation UI (handled by PM/design later).

Design notes summary:
- Golden families: group prompts into cohorts by intent and token-length buckets. Each family includes seeded perturbations (syntactic paraphrases, slot-value swaps) to expose sensitivity.
- Metric suite: combine a primary fidelity metric (token-level KL across logits after temperature matching) with secondary checks (top-1 divergence, BLEU-like n-gram recall, embedding cosine drift using reference encoder).
- Gate logic: evaluate each cohort independently; cohort pass requires primary_metric < cohort_threshold AND (secondary_metric_1 < sec_thresh_1 OR secondary_metric_2 > sec_thresh_2). Overall pass requires >= 90% cohorts passing or a weighted score above 0.92 depending on customer tier.
- Adaptive thresholds: thresholds are scaled by (1 + sqrt(mean_context_length / 256)) and adjusted by observed baseline drift from the unquantized reference run.

Telemetry and artifacts produced:
- Per-request telemetry: logits snapshot (first 64 tokens only), top-5 tokens, log-likelihood, embedding vector (64-dim compressed), latency, GPU config.
- Aggregates: cohort-level summary, failing examples with diff view, trend timeseries for primary metric.

Why different from existing harnesses: emphasis on contextual cohorting and adaptive thresholds (length-aware), deterministic logit-based primary metric (not just surface token checks), and explicit telemetry to Console for per-customer gating decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Prober can ingest a calibration profile (FP8/INT8) and run golden-family replay without manual intervention
Primary metric (token-level KL) computed for each request matches reference implementation within 1e-6 on sample cases
Cohort-level pass/fail logic implemented and results exported to telemetry with clear explainability (example diffs)
End-to-end job can be scheduled as a periodic CI check and completes within configured SLA (sample golden family of 10k prompts < 4h on dedicated test pool)
Console shows cohort pass/fail, trend charts, and links to failing examples for at least one test customer configuration
Unit tests and integration tests cover edge cases: empty context, extremely long contexts (>8k), deterministic RNG seeding for perturbations
implementation_plan: 2) Library: metric calculations (token-kl, top1-divergence, ngram recall, embedding drift) - PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1428 (WIP)
3) Golden family loader and perturbation bank with deterministic seeding - PR link will be attached to ticket
4) Runner: batch execution harness integrated with existing quant-eval job runner (extend ENG-273501 runner) - create sandbox pool for CI
5) Gate evaluator: implement adaptive threshold scaling and cohort aggregator to produce pass/fail and JSON explainers
6) Telemetry export: Console integration (runtime-telemetry -> console ingestion pipeline) and dashboard stubs
7) Smoke CI job and scheduled weekly run for critical customers
8) Postmortem and tuning week: iterate thresholds based on observed false positives/negatives
risks: Metric brittleness: models with identical semantics but different tokenization can trigger false failures; mitigated via embedding drift secondary checks
Compute cost: running full golden suites on large families is expensive; mitigations include sampling, early-stopping on cohort failures, and KV-cache reuse
Determinism: floating-point nondeterminism across GPU types may affect token-KL; mitigate by normalizing logits and adding epsilon floor plus deterministic seeding
Dataset leakage: golden prompts must avoid customer PII and be curated for licensing
